newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Former Bangladesh ruler asks party to vie for power.
newsitem.headline: Former Bangladesh ruler asks party to vie for power.

text.p: Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad, in his first public speech in the capital since being freed from jail in January, asked his followers on Tuesday to prepare to regain power.
"Organise yourselves and get ready for the next elections (due in 2001)," he told thousands of cheering supporters at a rally of his Jatiya Party in Dhaka.
But enthusiasm generated by the rally was deflated slightly after two top Jatiya leaders, Kazi Zafar Ahmed and Naziur Rahman Manju, nearly engaged in a fist fight on the dais.
They ignored Ershad's plea to calm down but were whisked away by angry party activists, witnesses said.

Ershad, however, continued his speech, telling the audience about the "inhumanly ordeal" he had suffered in captivity during the rule of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
Ershad, a retired army general who took power in a 1982 bloodless coup, was toppled in a 1990 popular uprising led by Khaleda and current Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of the Awami League.

Ershad's Jatiya Party, however, supported the Awami League to form a government after last June's general elections and Hasina appointed Ershad's trusted lieutenant Anwar Hossain as her communications minister.
BNP called it a "payback," which Ershad has rejected.
"My party is not the B-team of the Awami League. It's very much an independent entity," he said on Tuesday.
"We supported the government for it pledged to do good things for the nation. But that does not mean we will support their every action."
Trying further to reassert Jatiya's independent standing, Ershad said he was opposed to the government's plan to create a sub-regional economic cooperation forum with India, Nepal and Bhutan.
"Such a move would only undermine the SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation)," he said.
SAARC, launched in 1984, groups Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
